questions.question:
What is the grammatical role of the clause

"whose daring transcended mere athleticism"

options.text: Noun clause acting as the subject

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The clause **"whose daring transcended mere athleticism"** begins with the relative pronoun **"whose,"** which shows possession.
 
• This clause provides additional information about the noun **"figures."** In English grammar, a clause that functions like an adjective to modify or describe a noun or pronoun is called an **adjective clause** (or relative clause).
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** An adverbial clause modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb (usually answering when, where, why, or how). This clause describes a noun ("figures"), not the "history."
 
• **Option 3:** A noun clause acts as a subject or object (e.g., "What he said was true"). Here, the clause is modifying an existing noun.
 
• **Option 4:** An **adjective phrase** does not contain a subject and a finite verb. Since this has a subject ("daring") and a verb ("transcended"), it is a **clause**, not a phrase.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *For exams, identifying clause types is vital for error spotting. Remember that **"whose"** always introduces an adjective clause because it links a quality or possession back to the antecedent noun.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annals:** A record of events year by year; historical records.
 
• **Transcended:** Surpassed or went beyond the range or limits of.
 
• **Antecedent:** The noun or pronoun to which a relative pronoun refers (in this case, "figures").
 
• **Athleticism:** The physical qualities that are characteristic of athletes, such as strength, fitness, and agility.

questions.question:
What does the word "dialectic" most nearly imply in the phrase:

"...each ascent a dialectic between human fragility and the immutable majesty of the mountains" ?

options.text: A dialogue or interplay between opposing forces

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In philosophy and literature, a **"dialectic"** refers to the **interplay or tension between two opposing ideas** or forces that leads to a higher level of understanding or a new synthesis.
 
• In the context of the passage, the two opposing forces are **"human fragility"** (the weakness and mortality of the climber) and the **"immutable majesty"** (the unchanging, powerful nature of the mountain).
 
• The author is suggesting that mountaineering is not just a physical act, but a **dialogue or constant interaction** between these two extremes.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** A "silent observation" is passive; a dialectic implies an active, dynamic relationship.
 
• **Option 2:** While there is tension, the passage uses philosophical terms like "reverence" and "stewards," suggesting the relationship is deeper and more complex than a simple "hostile confrontation."
 
• **Option 4:** "Scientific measurement" is too literal and reductionist for a passage that focuses on "philosophical quests" and "introspection."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *For high-level exams, words like **"dialectic"** are used to move a discussion from the physical to the metaphysical. When you see "between X and Y," it almost always points to an interplay or relationship between those two variables.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Immutable:** Unchanging over time or unable to be changed.
 
• **Fragility:** The quality of being easily broken or damaged; here, it refers to human vulnerability.
 
• **Audacity:** A willingness to take bold risks.
 
• **Odyssey:** A long and eventful or adventurous journey or experience.

• In the context of the passage, **"immutable"** describes the majesty of the mountains as a contrast to **"human fragility."**
